resale_co.name: Certificate of Continued Occupancy, Certificate of Zoning Compliance and Certificate of Flood Damage Prevention Compliance (transfer of title)
resale_co.issued_by: City of Cape May Construction & Zoning Office (Construction Official, Zoning Officer and Floodplain Manager)
resale_co.lead_time: Apply at least 15 business days before the transfer of title
resale_co.valid_for: Certificate of continued occupancy and flood certificate: 2 years from issuance (the continued occupancy certificate expires on the date of transfer)
requirements: Certificate of Continued Occupancy (Code Section 199-7): inspection showing no work done without a construction permit, no open construction permits, and no unsafe or unsanitary conditions, blocked exits or fire hazards

Certificate of Zoning Compliance (Code Section 199-5): inspection confirming no change of use and that the use and number of units comply with the Zoning Ordinance; the certificate also gives notice of the property's historic district status

Certificate of Flood Damage Prevention Compliance (Code Section 199-6): checks the minimum number of flood vents; a flood elevation certificate must be submitted if the property is in a flood zone (one issued on or after January 1, 2010 is accepted)

Violations found must be fixed before closing, unless the buyer signs an acknowledgment, assumes the risk and agrees to fix them within 30 days (30 business days for the flood certificate) after closing

Exceptions: new construction with a certificate of occupancy issued within 2 years of the transfer, transfers without payment to a related person or entity, buyer certifies demolition within 90 days, and foreclosure transfers to a lender
Separate smoke/CO certificate from the Bureau of Fire Prevention (see fire certificate)

resale_co.how_to_apply: Submit the Certificate of Zoning Compliance Application (block, lot, zoning district, current and new owners, use, number of units, settlement date) and the Certificate of Flood Damage Prevention Compliance Application (with an elevation certificate if the property is in a flood zone), each with its fee, to the Construction & Zoning Office, City Hall, 643 Washington Street, Cape May, NJ 08204, at least 15 business days before closing. No separate Certificate of Continued Occupancy form was found online; ask the Construction Office (609-884-9555, construction@capemaycity.com) how to request it.

evidence.quote: Transfer of building, structures, or units. No person or entity shall sell or transfer title to any building, structure, portion of structure, or unit in a structure until such person or entity shall have first requested and obtained a certificate of continued occupancy certifying as follows:

The purpose of this section is to require an inspection of buildings, structures, or units prior to the transfer of title to determine (i) that there are no violations of law or orders of the Construction Official, and (ii) that no unsafe or unsanitary conditions have been found.

A certificate of continued occupancy shall be valid for two years from the date of issuance and shall expire on the date of transfer (subject to any obligation to correct any deficiencies post-closing).

Transfer of building, structures, or units. No person or entity shall sell or transfer title to any building, structure, portion of structure, or unit in a structure until such person or entity shall have first requested and obtained a certificate of zoning compliance certifying the following:
The fee for a Certificate of Zoning Compliance shall be $75.

All applications for a Certificate of Zoning Compliance, a Certificate of Compliance with Flood Damage Prevention Ordinance and Certificate of Continued Occupancy shall be submitted not less than 15 business days prior to the transfer of title.
The information below is necessary for the issuance of a Certificate of Zoning Compliance for the transfer of title to any building, structure or unit, within the City of Cape May.

No person or entity shall sell or transfer title to any building, structure, portion of structure, or unit in a structure until such person or entity shall have first requested and obtained a Certificate of Flood Damage Prevention Compliance.

resale_co.notes: City Code Chapter 199 (ecode360 CA1942, read in full through the print view) requires three certificates before title to any building or unit is sold or transferred: a Certificate of Zoning Compliance (Section 199-5, amended by Ord. No. 577-2025 on 10-7-2025), a Certificate of Flood Damage Prevention Compliance (Section 199-6) and a Certificate of Continued Occupancy (Section 199-7, added by Ord. No. 308-2016). The prior record only had the zoning certificate; the continued occupancy and flood certificates were missed. Fees: the City's zoning form (05/2018) and flood form (10/2017) each show $85, while the code (Section 199-8A(5) and (6)) still lists $75 for each; the forms are used here and the gap is an open question. The continued occupancy fee ($85 plus $50 per subcode inspection) is from the code only; no City form for it was found. Contacts: Construction Official Lou Vito Jr (609-884-9560, louv@capemaycity.com); Zoning Officer Bruce Britton (609-884-9556, bbritton@capemaycity.com); Technical Assistant Megan Long (609-884-9555, mlong@capemaycity.com); office email construction@capemaycity.com. The zoning form lists 609-884-9561, which the Construction page now shows as the Historic Preservation Commission line; the flood form lists 609-884-9545. The Fire Prevention Bureau's annual rental and business inspections (Ord. No. 364-2018, Section 247-9) are a rental program, not a resale requirement.

requirements: Sale of Property Form (created March 2025) still names the certificate as covering a portable fire extinguisher, but the Bureau's web page says fire extinguishers are no longer required in one- or two-family dwellings for sales or rentals; if one is kept it must be maintained (approved hanger, serviced within 12 months)
Smoke alarms no older than 10 years; battery-only smoke alarms must be the 10-year sealed battery type (listed on the Bureau page as top rental violations)
Carbon monoxide alarm near sleeping areas and on every level when there are fuel-burning appliances, an attached garage or a fireplace

authorities.how_to_apply: Fill out the Sale of Property Form (check the Certificate of Smoke Alarm, Carbon Monoxide Alarm option for 1-2 family dwellings, give the closing date and agent/title contact) and send it to the Bureau of Fire Prevention, fireprevention@capemaycity.com, 609-884-9599. Do not send payment with the application; the fee is set when the form is received and the Bureau invoices it (fire invoices can be paid online through the City's Tyler portal).

fire_cert.notes: The City is the local fire enforcing agency (DCA registry code M). Fees are printed on the Bureau's Sale of Property Form (PDF created 2025-03-18) and match City Code Section 247-8 (amended 2-19-2025 by Ord. No. 549-2025), which also says the certificate is valid 180 days from inspection and is not transferable. The form also lists a Status of Fire Code letter at $125.00 for other uses (multiple dwellings, hotels, businesses); that is not the 1-2 family certificate. The Bureau office is at 712 Washington Street in the fire house. Other staff: Administrative Clerk Nancy Mohan (609-884-9599, fireprevention@capemaycity.com); Fire Inspectors Chris Larcombe (609-957-5382) and Casey Hunt (609-957-5318). The form and the code section title still name a portable fire extinguisher, but the Bureau page says extinguishers are no longer required in 1-2 family homes for sales or rentals (P.L.2025, c.19).

other_items.label: Certificate of Zoning Compliance and Certificate of Flood Damage Prevention Compliance
other_items.detail: Both are required before transfer of title along with the Certificate of Continued Occupancy (see resale_co). The flood certificate needs a flood elevation certificate if the property is in a flood zone.

other_items.label: Open construction permits
other_items.detail: The Certificate of Continued Occupancy certifies there are no open construction permits and no work done without a permit, so open permits should be closed before closing.
